description: OFF-BALL: MAKE A STARTED RUN COMMIT FOR HALF A SECOND INSTEAD OF A FIFTH. Two re-aims, one in ActionSelectorChanceSpaceRun::vf3 (0x143df72d0) and one in ActionSelectorDiagonalRun::vf3 (0x143e05130). WHAT vf3 IS. The manager update 0x143d52470 was read instruction by instruction. It has two passes over its selector array (16-byte entries at mgr+0x1720, count at mgr+0x218). PASS 1 (loop at 0x143d526c0): for every team-mate slot whose currently assigned action id [teamAI+0x8f4c+slot*4] equals this selector's own id [sel+0x128], it calls sel->vf3(ctx, playerIdx) through vtable+0x18, and if vf3 returns TRUE it calls 0x1442edf70(teamAI, slot), which CLEARS the assignment. PASS 2 (loop at 0x143d52794): each selector's vf2 (the dispatcher 0x143df1080) then refills the slots that were freed. So vf3 is the 'should this run stop now?' test, and it is the whole of the game's run hysteresis. THE TIMER. Both vf3s compute elapsed = [rec+8] - [rec+4] from the per-slot action record (teamAI + 0x8f78 + slot*0x34, fetched by 0x1442eda20) and compare it against int(fps*0.2 + 0.5) - 12 frames at 60 fps. ChanceSpaceRun: 0x143df73a8 multiplies the fps global by the 0.2f cell, then 0x143df73bd 'cmp ebx,ecx; jae' goes to the further checks, and the short-of-timer path returns 'keep' unless a second predicate (0x143d2f710) fires. DiagonalRun: 0x143e051b2 multiplies by the same 0.2f cell, then 0x143e051c7 'cmp ebx,eax; jb 0x143e051de' where 0x143e051de is 'xor al,al' = do not abort. Below the threshold the run is protected; above it, it is re-tested every frame. Re-aiming the 0.2f read to the existing 0.5f cell lengthens the protected window to about 30 frames. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: the hard aborts are unconditional and are NOT gated by this timer. In DiagonalRun they are match state != 1 (0x143e05148), [teamCtx+0x28d] == 0 (0x143e05163) and 'the runner has become the ball holder' (0x143e0516c, 'cmp [ctx+0x1c], edi'). A run still dies instantly when the ball arrives or play stops. All this lever changes is the twitchy re-evaluation in between. WHY BOTHER: the manager runs for a team every second frame (guard at 0x143d03464: '[match+0x3318] & 1 == teamIdx'; [match+0x3318] is the match FRAME COUNTER - many sites compute 'frame - storedStamp' and compare the difference against an fps-derived frame count, e.g. 0x143c59c82 'sub eax,[rbx+0x10]; cmp eax,3'), so past 0.2 s the game asks 'stop this run?' about 30 times a second. Because the scoring is completely deterministic - no RNG on any selector path, from a 6-level global call-graph search over 943,597 direct call edges against all five of the image's LCG cores, with two positive controls - the answer is usually the same and the run continues; but when the geometry is marginal a run can be dropped and restarted repeatedly, which reads on screen as a runner checking and re-checking instead of going. TEST THIS ONE ON ITS OWN. It is the only pack here whose effect is a feel change rather than a count change, and the easiest to be wrong about: the flicker may come from the ABORT predicates (0x143e8a970 for DiagonalRun, 0x143d2f710 for ChanceSpaceRun) rather than from the window length, and neither was decoded. An honest result here may be 'no visible difference'. WHO: everyone - no human/CPU test exists anywhere on the manager's sole call path (0x143d03493 is the only reference to 0x143d52470 in the image). EVIDENCE: (b) unambiguous disassembly of the two-pass structure, both timers and the abort conditions; (a) emulation only for the RNG search; (c) inferred that 0.5 s is the right size rather than 0.3 or 1.0 - nothing in the code suggests a value, this is a judgement call. BYTES: both instructions are byte-identical in the PRISTINE backup and the installed exe. The destination 0x147850248 is the plain 0.5f cell in .tls$: non-writable, writers=0, 7052 referrers - which is precisely why it is used only as a READ target and never edited in place. Same instruction length; no pool cell is written. Revert: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/offball-run-commit.json
